title: Relief from Cart Path for a Left-Handed Stance
question: A right-handed player's ball comes to rest beside a tree, blocking any reasonable right-handed stroke. The player could reasonably play the ball left-handed. In taking a left-handed stance, their feet are on an artificially surfaced cart path. Is the player entitled to free relief from the cart path?

choices.text: Yes, provided the left-handed stroke is reasonable in the circumstances.
No, free relief is not allowed because the player is right-handed.
No, free relief cannot be taken for a stance used only to seek relief.
Yes, but only if their clubs are designed for left-handed play.

explanation: Under Rule 16.1, a player is entitled to free relief from an immovable obstruction, such as a cart path, if it interferes with the player’s area of intended stance or swing. If playing left-handed is a reasonable stroke in the circumstances, interference for a left-handed stroke entitles the player to relief, even if the player is usually right-handed. After taking relief for the left-handed stance, the player is not required to play the next stroke left-handed if a right-handed stroke is possible from the new lie.

juniorVersion.title: Can I get free relief from a path if I have to hit left-handed?
juniorVersion.question: Your golf ball stops next to a tree, and you can't hit it right-handed because the tree is in the way. You can try a left-handed shot, but if you stand that way, your feet are on the hard path. Can you take your ball off the path for free?

choices.text: Yes, if the left-handed shot is a good idea for your ball.
No, you can’t because you are a right-handed player.
No, you can’t take relief just by changing how you stand.
Yes, but only if you have a left-handed club.

juniorVersion.explanation: You can get free relief from the hard path if you need to stand on it for a left-handed shot, even if you are usually right-handed. The left-handed shot has to make sense for the place your ball is. After you move your ball, you can still hit it right-handed if you want.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: You can move your ball away from something like a path without any penalty.
Something made by people, like a path or a bench.
How you stand to hit your ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show how you can stand left-handed or right-handed and point out when your feet are on the path. Let children try both ways to see when free relief is allowed.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they can only get relief for the way they usually play.
Some might think they must use a left-handed club to get relief.
They might believe you always have to hit the next shot the same way you were standing for relief.
